subject: german
title: Stamp 3: Treuhand and the East-West Gap
welcome_lead: Stamp the economic transformation of the East and lingering divides.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on the Treuhand, economic transition, and East-West differences today.

concepts.def: Agency 1990-1994 privatising former DDR state enterprises (Volkseigene Betriebe).
Reconstruction East; large transfer programme to modernise eastern infrastructure.
Solidarity surcharge introduced 1991 to finance reunification.
Nostalgia for DDR life, often expressed through products like Ampelmannchen.
People's enterprise; the dominant form of state-owned firm in the DDR.
East Germany today; lower wages, higher unemployment, and continued political divergence.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Treuhandanstalt inherited about 8,500 firms employing four million people. It privatised, restructured, or closed them by 1994. Critics blamed it for mass unemployment in the east.
The 2003 film Good Bye, Lenin! captured Ostalgie humorously. Eastern brands (Rotkappchen sparkling wine, Trabant cars, Ampelmannchen) became cult objects.
Even decades later, average wages and pensions in the east trail western levels by roughly 10-20%. Political behaviour also differs: the AfD and Linke perform better in the east.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between 'ich will' and 'ich möchte'?
options: Ich will is future tense.
Ich will = I want (strong, direct); ich möchte = I would like (polite).
Bold.
They mean the same thing.
